title: Bug report: strict single-precision floating point comparisons (flt.s) may return 1 even though the operands are equal
body:
Hi there!

I've detected a bug in VexRiscv.

## Brief bug description

The instruction `flt.s` must return `0` when the two operands are equal. Under certain conditions, it returns `1` even though the operands are equal.

## Example instance

### Snippet

Here is an example RISC-V (rv32imfd) snippet:
```
  .section ".text.init","ax",@progbits
  .globl _start
  .align 2
_start:
  # Enable the FPU
  li t0, 0x2000
  csrs mstatus, t0
  csrw	fcsr,x0

  li t0, 0xFFFFFFFF
  fcvt.s.wu	ft0,t0,rtz

  la t0, .fdata0
  fld ft1, 0(t0)

  // Here, ft0 = ft1 = 0xffffffff4f7fffff

  flt.s	t0,ft1,ft0

  li t2, 0x10
  sw t0, 0(t2)

  sw x0, (x0)

infinite_loop:
  jal	x0,infinite_loop

.section ".fdata0","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff4f7fffff
```

### Expected and actual results

We expect `t0 = 0`. I verified this with Spike.
However,  VexRiscv returns `t0 = 1`.

## Notes

This issue has commonalities with #316 . The FPU seems to have a strict ordering between the two floating-point registers, which are in fact equal.

Thanks!
Flavien

fix_commits.messageHeadline: Fix FPU with F64 support, not removing mantissa precision from F32 #317

comments.body: Looking at the wave, the issue is before the flt.s, so either fcvt, either fld. i'm looking a tit.
Seems like it is due to fcvt storing too much precision bits in the register file.

https://github.com/SpinalHDL/VexRiscv/commit/5f67075e3094f1f31b7fe9f480e08fc5c32b28c3 Seems to fix it.

Thanks :D
Cool! Well, thank you for your reactivity! I would not be surprised if it also fixed some other bugs in the batch.
So yes, most of the issues were directly related to this :)

title: Potential Bug in BPU on s2_fire_dup?
body:
### Before start

- [x] I have read the [RISC-V ISA Manual](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-isa-manual) and this is not a RISC-V ISA question. 我已经阅读过 RISC-V 指令集手册，这不是一个指令集本身的问题。

- [X] I have reviewed the commit messages from the relevant commit history. 我已经浏览过相关的提交历史和提交信息。

### Describe the bug

Sorry If I was wrong, but I noticed that `s2_fire_dup` is assigned twice in the BPU.scala:
```
  for (
    (((s2_fire, s3_components_ready), s3_ready), s2_valid) <-
      s2_fire_dup zip s3_components_ready_dup zip s3_ready_dup zip s2_valid_dup
  )
    s2_fire := s2_valid && s3_components_ready && s3_ready
```
and 
```
  s2_fire_dup := s2_valid_dup
```

The second assignment completely overwrites the first one, relying only on s2_valid but not on the `s3_components_ready` and `s3_ready` signals.

Is this supposed to happen?
Jerry

### Expected behavior

It should be `s2_fire := s2_valid && s3_components_ready && s3_ready`

### To Reproduce

Issue at file: xiangshan/frontend/BPU.scala around line 403-415


### Environment

- XiangShan branch: Master
- XiangShan commit id: 844fba5b86d00c2ec233eddeffc3d637862575fd
- NEMU commit id: Not Used
- SPIKE commit id: Not Used

_No response_

title: CJALR with instr[14:12] != 0 is not illegal
body:
The decoder for CJALR will not raise an illegal instruction exception when `instr[14:12] != 0`, but it will also not set `cheri_jalr_en`:

https://github.com/microsoft/cheriot-ibex/blob/3f0ec8600cb7621c4c952951d211b3515116ea27/rtl/ibex_decoder.sv#L343-L367

When a CJALR instruction is run with `instr[14:12] != 0`, the instruction that runs becomes one which stores the next instruction PC to the register file, but does not branch, since it runs into the old logic for JALR. This is therefore not a security issue, but is a bug.

Instead `illegal_insn` should be set when `instr[14:12] != 0` (see the original code for JALR, which does the same).

title: PoR value of MSTATUS
body:
### Bug Description

The [documented](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cve2/blob/b8c94a3e84087e230581fcdddadbea398ea19a7e/doc/03_reference/cs_registers.rst?plain=1#LL109C1-L109C1) power-on-reset value of the `mstatus` CSR (0x300) is 0x0000_1800 which expands to:

| Bit Pos  | PoR | Field     |
| ------- | ----- | -------------- |
| 21    | 1'b0  | **TW**  |
| 17    | 1'b0 | **MPRV**  |
| 12:11 | 2'b11  | **MPP**  |
| 7     | 1'b0  | **MPIE** |
| 3     | 1'b0  | **MIE**  |

However the coded PoR in the [RTL](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cve2/blob/b8c94a3e84087e230581fcdddadbea398ea19a7e/rtl/cve2_cs_registers.sv#L745) is:
```
localparam status_t MSTATUS_RST_VAL = '{mie:  1'b0,
                                          mpie: 1'b1,
                                          mpp:  PRIV_LVL_U,
                                          mprv: 1'b0,
                                          tw:   1'b0};
```
Given that [PRIV_LVL_U](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cve2/blob/b8c94a3e84087e230581fcdddadbea398ea19a7e/rtl/cve2_pkg.sv#L206) is 2'b00, this yields a PoR of 0x0000_0080.

I believe that the documented PoR value is the proper one, but the coded PoR has been in the Ibex code for three years so I am not certain.

You can show this in simulation in CORE-V-VERIF by running the `debug_test`:
```
$ make test TEST=debug_test
```
(Set the SIMULATOR and USE_ISS vars as appropriate for your installation.)

fix_commits.messageHeadline: fix #128 power-on-reset value for MSTATUS CSR
Merge pull request #129 from NXP/bug/por-value-of-mstatus

comments.body: Note that the lowRISC team has determined that for Ibex, this is a _documentation_ bug, not an RTL bug.  See [Ibex Issue #2054](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/issues/2054).  While I agree with their interpretation, I recommend we treat this as an RTL issue and proceed with @szbieg's update in [CVE2 pull-request #129](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cve2/pull/129/files).  This will align the PoR state of the CVE2 cores with the CV32E40 cores.

title: sync/async/flush reset condition in lsu_cappuccino
body:
https://github.com/openrisc/mor1kx/blob/master/rtl/verilog/mor1kx_lsu_cappuccino.v#L524

``` verilog
always @(posedge clk)
     if (rst | pipeline_flush_i)
       atomic_reserve <= 0;
     else if (ctrl_op_lsu_store_i & ctrl_op_lsu_atomic_i & write_done ||
          !ctrl_op_lsu_atomic_i & store_buffer_write &
          (store_buffer_wadr == atomic_addr) ||
          (snoop_valid & (snoop_adr_i == atomic_addr)))
       atomic_reserve <= 0;
```

`(rst | pipeline_flush_i)` seems a bit dodgy if the timing tools were to analyse the net as an asyncronous reset (in other parts of the code) and synchronous here.  Maybe it's ok (who knows with fpga design tools!), though `pipeline_flush_i` could migrate, I think, to the first if condition and possibly a `OR_ASYNC_RST` added to the `always @` trigger.

### Bug Description

If the `in` input to the [std_cache_pkg::one_hot_to_bin()](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/513bb91f823a18a6653a1685acd60408049c9c8f/core/include/std_cache_pkg.sv#L78) function is 0 and  `ariane_pkg::DCACHE_SET_ASSOC` is a power of 2 then this function enters an infinite loop since the loop variable`i` wraps from DCACHE_SET_ASSOC-1 to 0 and the loop condition is always true.

title: Endianness in WishboneDMAReader
body:
Hi,

Shouldn't this be opposite ? 
https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/blob/78c1751c4781ffe156128748810ee4af85fee058/litex/soc/cores/dma.py#L19-L20

Just to try this out I used the `WishboneDMAReader` in a module of my SoC (with vexriscv) simulation to read a word from SRAM and print it in my C code and it printed reversed. The complete system is little endian.
```
DMA Read from : 0x10003fac
Readback from DMA: 0xdf0feca
Actual value : 0xcafef00d
```

with the format_bytes reversed
```python
 def format_bytes(s, endianness): 
     return {"little": s, "big": reverse_bytes(s)}[endianness]
```
the print is as expected

```
DMA Read from : 0x10003fac
Readback from DMA: 0xcafef00d
Actual value : 0xcafef00d
```

fix_commits.messageHeadline: dma: add explicit byte-swap control

comments.body:
Hi @navaneeth-cirel,

this probably similar to https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litedram/issues/251. There is a endianness mismatch between the model and real hardware. I'll try to address this soon.

Hi @enjoy-digital ,

After brief look at the issue referenced it seems that there is a mismatch between the simulation and target hardware, but in my case I am seeing the mismatch in Simulation itself.
Just to give more clarity , what I am doing is writing a 32bit value to a `uint32_t` variable in the C code and set its address to the DMA to read and transfer to a CSR status register which I am then reading and printing in the C code, where the mismatch is observed.

I re-checked the current code and your observation still makes sense for a direct word-level use of `WishboneDMAReader`.

For a little-endian CPU writing `0xcafef00d` as a `uint32_t`, the Wishbone word read back by the DMA is already `0xcafef00d`. Passing `endianness="little"` to `WishboneDMAReader` then applies `reverse_bytes()`, so a direct word consumer such as a CSR status register will see `0x0df0feca`.

So for raw word-oriented use, the DMA should be instantiated with `endianness="big"` / no byte swap.

I would avoid flipping the global `format_bytes()` mapping since the DMA is also used in byte-stream storage paths, where this conversion is part of the expected byte ordering. The real issue is that the parameter is confusing for direct word users, so we should probably document this better and/or add a clearer no-swap/raw mode in the future.

This has now been improved with:  c4baeb3e1a3a35ecaa3e47eae4d2951b64d76bdd

The existing DMA endianness behavior is kept for compatibility: `endianness="little"` still byte-swaps and `endianness="big"` still preserves the raw Wishbone word.

To make direct word-oriented use cases clearer, `WishboneDMAReader` and `WishboneDMAWriter` now also have an explicit `with_byteswap` override. So for a raw word transfer such as the `0xcafef00d` case discussed here, the DMA can now be instantiated with:

```python
  WishboneDMAReader(bus, endianness="little", with_byteswap=False)
```

This preserves the raw Wishbone word instead of byte-swapping it.

I also added regression coverage for the reported word-level case on both reader and writer, checking both the legacy little-endian byte-swap behavior and the explicit no-swap path.

I also added a follow-up test commit to double-check the default behavior: https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/commit/db2678d1a2df8f47c76510fec134c4a093cf45cc

This adds regression coverage for the storage-style byte-stream path used by LiteSDCard/LiteSATA, where DMA words are converted to/from 8-bit streams with reverse stream converters.

The tests confirm why the legacy default remains unchanged for these users, while raw word-oriented users can use the explicit `with_byteswap=False` override added above.

With the explicit `with_byteswap=False` override and the added regression tests for both raw word and byte-stream DMA paths, I think this is now covered. Closing, but please reopen or open a follow-up if another DMA endianness case still behaves unexpectedly.

title: Should the default JTAG IDCODE be 0x1?
body:
https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/9002e7e53299598027f41b95dba1666310923699/src/main/scala/rocketchip/DebugTransport.scala#L22

```scala
class JtagDTMKeyDefault extends JtagDTMConfig(
  idcodeVersion = 0,
  idcodePartNum = 0,
  idcodeManufId = 0,
debugIdleCycles = 5) // Reasonable guess for synchronization.
```

Should the default IDCODE be 0x1, or the same as in the previous debug module (0x10e31913)? Or should it throw an error message to prevent rocket from elaborating if the JTAG is enabled but the idcode is not specified?

@mwachs5 @palmer-dabbelt @ducky64

fix_commits.messageHeadline: Add a note to wire up jtag_mfr_id
Add a note to wire up jtag_mfr_id (#778)

comments.body:
The IDCODE (0x10e31913) uses SiFive's assigned JEDEC Manufacturer ID. So in general those who aren't SiFive should not be using that IDCODE. That's why we removed it from the default.

Those using rocket-chip repo should probably override this default value to something meaningful for their design. The ManufId is actually exported from the ExampleTop as part of its I/O and is tied off in the TestHarness.

I see, that makes sense. Thanks for the explanation. Would having an elaboration-time warning for users of rocket-chip be useful so that they don't run into surprises when they try to program their cores?

When you say "program their cores" do you mean when using OpenOCD to communicate with them? Is there actually a value that you use there that causes a problem? riscv-openocd is very tolerant of the IDCODE, it may print a warning if it's not the expected ID.

I'm not sure what the elaboration time warning would be because the mfr_id could go all the way out the pins of the chip. I added a runtime warning (so if you ran with simulate it could at least detect illegal idcodes, though the chances you detect an unconnected mfr_id are somewhat low):

https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/master/src/main/scala/jtag/JtagTap.scala#L175

Note that if you did actually use the defaults here, then your IDCODE *would* be 0x1, because there is a bit in the IDCODE "always 1":
https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/master/src/main/scala/rocketchip/DebugTransport.scala#L230

@mwachs5 Ah, I see. I think I see where my confusion was coming from now.

In https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/9002e7e53299598027f41b95dba1666310923699/src/main/scala/rocketchip/DebugTransport.scala#L231 it uses two out of the three `Int`s in `JtagDTMConfig` but doesn't actually 
use the third one. I was confused since I thought that all 3 would be determined at elaboration-time by `JtagDTMConfig`. In my design, I think I left io.jtag_mfr_id unconnected and the synthesis tool tied it at some point to zero.

Perhaps if we are not actually going to use `c.idcodeManufId.U`, perhaps it could be a good idea to put in a comment saying "Please wire up io.jtag_mfr_id to set the mfr_id or something"? The TestHarness I think manually goes and re-retrieves it (or maybe just remove `idcodeManufId` from `JtagDTMConfig` to avoid confusion perhaps).

```scala
  idcode.always1    := 1.U
  idcode.version    := c.idcodeVersion.U
  idcode.partNumber := c.idcodePartNum.U
  idcode.mfrId := io.jtag_mfr_id
```

The comment seems like a reasonable request. Keep in mind that RocketChipExampleTop is just an example top level, and other designs could actually wire up mfrId using the value in JtagDTMConfig,  I think we should leave it there but comment it as you suggest.
Thoughts on https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/pull/778 ?

title: Bug report: dependent arithmetic/muldiv single-precision operations cause wrong output by more than +1 or -1
body:
Hi there!

I've detected a bug in VexRiscv, similar to #315 but the mismatch may be larger than +1 or -1.

## Brief bug description

A pair of dependent single-precision floating arithmetic/muldiv operations (not necessarily immediately following each other), provides wrong results in some cases, differing from the expectation by potentially a magnitude above 1.

I ran this code on master (b29eb54) where I cherry-picked the fix 5f67075, with the configuration described in #318 .

## Snippet

Here is an example RISC-V (rv32imfd) snippet:
```
  .section ".text.init","ax",@progbits
  .globl _start
  .align 2
_start:
  # Enable the FPU
  li t0, 0x2000
  csrs mstatus, t0
  csrw	fcsr,x0

  la t0, .fdata0
  fld fa2, (t0)
  la t0, .fdata1
  fld ft7, (t0)

  fdiv.s	fs0,ft7,fa2,rmm
  fmul.s	fa2,fs0,fa2,rdn

  li t0, 0x18
  fsd fa2, 0(t0)

  sw x0, (x0)

infinite_loop:
  jal	x0,infinite_loop

.section ".fdata0","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff5f4135ef # fa2
.section ".fdata1","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff98e7d58f # ft7
```

### Expected and actual results

We expect `fa2= 0xffffffff98e7b3ae`. I verified this with Spike.
However,  VexRiscv returns `fa2 = 0xffffffff98e7d58f`.

Thanks!
Flavien

title: [BUG] UnalignQueue "enqPtr < deqPtr" assertion triggered by cross-16B sd under sbuffer-stride pressure
body:
### Before start

- [x] I have read the [RISC-V ISA Manual](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-isa-manual) and this is not a RISC-V ISA question. 我已经阅读过 RISC-V 指令集手册，这不是一个指令集本身的问题。
- [x] I have read the [XiangShan Documents](https://xiangshan-doc.readthedocs.io/zh_CN/latest). 我已经阅读过香山文档。
- [x] I have searched the previous issues and did not find anything relevant. 我已经搜索过之前的 issue，并没有找到相关的。
- [x] I have reviewed the commit messages from the relevant commit history. 我已经浏览过相关的提交历史和提交信息。
- [x] I have reproduced the incorrect behaviors using the latest commit on the master branch. 我已经使用 master 分支最新的 commit 复现了不正确的行为。

### Branch

kunminghu-v3

### Describe the bug

A short loop of cross-16B `sd` stores with unique-line stride deterministically fires the assertion at `NewStoreQueue.scala:1414` inside the inner `UnalignQueue` module:

```scala
XSError(enqPtr < deqPtr && !full, s"Something wrong in UnalignQueue!")
```

```
[0] %Error: UnalignQueue.sv:139: Assertion failed in
    TOP.SimTop.cpu.l_soc.core_with_l2.core.memBlock.inner_lsq.storeQueue.unalignQueue:
    Assertion failed at LogUtils.scala:132
%Error: build/rtl/UnalignQueue.sv:139: Verilog $stop
Aborting...
```

The reproducer (200 iterations, two cross-16B `sd`s per iteration, 32-byte stride) fires the assertion deterministically within 5,000 cycles (5/5 reruns). Halving the iteration count, removing the stride, removing the second `sd`, or aligning the base address each makes the assertion not fire in the same cycle window.

### Expected behavior

`UnalignQueue` should maintain its `enqPtr` / `deqPtr` invariant under any legal sequence of cross-16B stores, regardless of sbuffer occupancy or loop-trip count.

### Environment

- Hardware
  - CPU: Intel Xeon Platinum 8592+
  - Memory (GB): 1006
  - Storage (GB): 2000
- Software
  - Operating system: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS
  - gcc version: 13.2.0
  - clang version: -
  - java version: openjdk 21.0.10
  - mill version: 0.12.15
- Repo
  - XiangShan commit id: `cc942e98c8fdd4b0ad3a8bddc9bfbd125b1f5d81`
  - difftest commit id: `f9d0bb858c18133984a5efd476f59989c69cb23f`
  - NEMU commit id: not used (`--no-diff`)
  - SPIKE commit id: not used
- Build & Run
  - Build command: `make sim-verilog && make -C ./difftest emu NUM_CORES=1 RTL_SUFFIX=sv`
  - Run command: `./build/verilator-compile/emu --no-diff -i unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.bin -C 5000`

### To Reproduce

Run the attached binary:

```
./build/verilator-compile/emu --no-diff -i unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.bin -C 5000
```

The assertion fires deterministically before 5,000 cycles (5/5 reruns).

The full reproducer is 9 instructions:

```assembly
_start:
  li   s2, 200                  # iteration count
  li   t0, 0x8010000F           # base; offset 15 -> cross-16B sd
  li   t3, 0xDEADBEEF
  li   t5, 32                   # unique-line stride
.Lloop:
  sd   t3, 0(t0)                # first  cross-16B sd
  sd   t3, 16(t0)               # second cross-16B sd
  add  t0, t0, t5
  addi s2, s2, -1
  bnez s2, .Lloop
```

To rebuild from the attached `.S`:

```bash
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -nostdlib -nostartfiles -static \
    -march=rv64g -mabi=lp64 -T link.ld \
    -o unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.elf unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.S
riscv64-unknown-elf-objcopy -O binary unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.elf unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.bin
```

`link.ld` is a one-line linker script placing `.text` at `0x80000000`.

[unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27475354/unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.zip) — contains the `.S`, the pre-built `.bin`, the linker script, and the failing run log.

### Additional context

_No response_

title: phy/ecp5rgmii: Incorrect parameters in DELAYF blocks
body:
In some recent debugging I've discovered that nextpnr does not consider strings such as `"DELAY80"` a valid parameter value for `DEL_VALUE` 

See in this snippet, taken from the ecp5rgmii phy

```python
rx_delay_taps = 80

self.specials += [
       Instance("DELAYF",
                p_DEL_MODE  = "SCLK_ALIGNED",
                p_DEL_VALUE = "DELAY{}".format(rx_delay_taps),
                i_LOADN     = 1,
                i_MOVE      = 0,
                i_DIRECTION = 0,
                i_A         = pads.rx_ctl,
                o_Z         = rx_ctl_delayf),
]
```

This results in a design where all the IO_DELAY blocks are set to the same value. 
(The value set is actually 50 rather than 0 because of the `SCLK_ALIGNED` mode see nextpnr code [here](https://github.com/YosysHQ/nextpnr/blob/576baa994f4b9e1746a231469bfd9e65d1d5a2b4/ecp5/pack.cc#L1981) )

This creates a design that sometimes runs, but sometimes does not run because the timing is very marginal.

title: [F2I BUG] FP64 to UINT32 cast incorrectly raises NX instead of NV for large negative inputs that wrap to zero after rounding
body:
## Bug description
Inputs to reproduce the bug which concerns the `fpnew_cast_multi` unit

```
operands_i  = 0xc1effffffffbffff  // FP64 negative value
op_i        = F2I
op_mod_i    = 1                   // unsigned cast
src_fmt_i   = FP64
int_fmt_i   = INT32
rnd_mode_i  = RNE
```

Expected Output (computed by reference model [cvfpu-uvm](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu-uvm))
```
result_o = 0x00000000
status_o.NV = 1    // invalid operation: negative float cast to unsigned
status_o.NX = 0
```
Actual Output
```
result_o = 0x00000000
status_o.NV = 0    // missing
status_o.NX = 1    // incorrectly raised
```
## Root cause
The first check is done at this stage
https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/a74d99a32bd11ce0b05a82b0d6d26f98df3bba65/src/fpnew_cast_multi.sv#L445-L450
The input unbiased exponent of `31` is just below the `of_before_round` threshold for uint32 `(INT_WIDTH - 1 + op_mod = 32)`, so no pre-rounding overflow is detected and the value proceeds through the normal cast path.

With `denorm_shamt = MAX_INT_WIDTH - 1 - input_exp_q = 0`, the integer part fills all 32 bits:
```
final_int            = 0xFFFFFFFF
round_sticky_bits    = 2'b11       // R=1, S=1
```
With `RNE`  rounding mode and `RS = 2'b11 `(strictly greater than 1/2 ulp), `fpnew_rounding` unit sets `round_up = 1`.

This causes the absolute rounded value to wrap (overflow):
`abs_rounded_o = 0xFFFFFFFF + 1 = 0x100000000 → truncated to 0x00000000`

https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/a74d99a32bd11ce0b05a82b0d6d26f98df3bba65/src/fpnew_cast_multi.sv#L623

`rounded_int_res_zero` is wrongly set to 1.

This corrupts the only remaining guard for the negative-to-unsigned special case:
https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/a74d99a32bd11ce0b05a82b0d6d26f98df3bba65/src/fpnew_cast_multi.sv#L729-L732

```
assign int_result_is_special = ...
    (input_sign_q & op_mod_q2 & ~rounded_int_res_zero);
//   1            & 1         & ~1                      = 0  ← not triggered
```

With `of_before_round = 0`, `of_after_round` skipped (negative sign guard), and `int_result_is_special = 0`, the result takes the normal path, producing the correct value `0x00000000` by coincidence but raising **NX** instead of **NV**.

title: Wrong parameter value assigned to PageAddrWidth of idma_legalizer_page_splitter in idma_legalizer.sv.tpl?
body:
I've been running into an issue synthesizing idma_legalizer_page_splitter in the block below. It is saying that `i` is out of range
```
  always_comb begin : proc_range_select
        page_offset = '0;
        for (int i = 0; i < PageAddrWidth; i++) begin
            page_offset[i] = page_addr_width > i ? addr_i[i] : 1'b0;
        end
    end
```
The discrepancy seems to be in idma_legalizer.sv.tpl. The instantiation of idma_legalizer_page_splitter has parameter `PageAddrWidth` set to PageSize, but it passes in `page_addr_t` which has a width of $clog2(PageSize). 
  ```
  idma_legalizer_page_splitter #(
        .OffsetWidth   ( OffsetWidth ),
        .PageAddrWidth ( PageSize    ),
        .addr_t        ( addr_t      ),
        .page_len_t    ( page_len_t  ),

title: [BUG] fcvt.s.d misses UF on boundary cases that round to the minimum normal single
body:
CVA6 reports incorrect fflags for a boundary fcvt.s.d case. The converted single-precision result matches Spike, but the underflow flag is missing.

I reproduced this on current master (02e11e3b9d9e6a087dc4811b933bf0cc80156e1a) with cv64a6_imafdc_sv39, using spike vs veri-testharness.

The minimal case is:

- input: 0x380fffffe0000000
- instruction: fcvt.s.d
- rounding mode: RNE

Both Spike and CVA6 produce the same final single-precision result:

But fflags differ:
- Spike: 0x03 (NX|UF)
- CVA6 RTL: 0x01 (NX)

Observed mismatch:
```
Mismatch[1]:
spike[1427] : pc[0000000080003020] csrrs   t2, fflags, zero: t2:0000000000000003
veri-testharness[1427] : pc[0000000080003020] csrrs   t2, fflags, zero: t2:0000000000000001
```

So this is not a wrong-result bug. The result value itself matches. The issue is that UF is not reported.

We suspect the RTL design file causing the error is fpnew_cast_multi.sv, where uf_after_round only checks whether the rounded exponent field is 0, missing the carry from denormal to min normal.

Minimal reproducer:
```
  .section .text
  .globl main
  main:
    li   t0, 0
    csrw frm, t0

    li   t0, 0x380fffffe0000000
    fmv.d.x ft0, t0

    csrw fflags, x0
    fcvt.s.d ft1, ft0
    fmv.x.w  t1, ft1
    csrr     t2, fflags

    li   a0, 0
    jal  exit
```

fix_commits.messageHeadline: fpnew_cast_multi: Fix underflow detection logic at subnormal-nomal

0077d9e buggy code before fix  commit cb3f0e5:

|                                    | Value                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| **CEX input**                      | `0x380FFFFFD0000002` (RUP)                             |
| **FP64 true exponent**             | −127 = FP32 emin − 1 ✓                                 |
| **FP32 pre-round 23-bit fraction** | `0x7FFFFF` = all 23 bits 1 ✓                           |
| **Rounding action**                | `0x7FFFFF + 1 = 0x800000` → carry out → exponent 0 → 1 |
| **RTL result**                     | `0x00800000` (numerically correct)                     |
| **RTL fflags**                     | `0x01` (NX only — **UF missing**)                      |
| **Spec fflags**                    | `0x03` (NX\|UF — correct)                              |

### Exact the same cornel scene

1. **Condition 1** — exp of original result = emin−1 = −127 (FP32) ✓  
2. **Condition 2** — first N=23 explicit fraction bits all 1s (`0x7FFFFF`) ✓

title: VCK5000 ES1: kernel hangs at vx_ready_wait despite XRT AFU done handshake fix (related to #262, #263, #278)
body:
# VCK5000 ES1: kernel hangs at `vx_ready_wait` despite XRT AFU done handshake fix (related to #262, #263, #278)

## Summary

On Xilinx VCK5000 ES1 (Versal), Vortex kernels uploaded successfully via the
XRT runtime hang indefinitely at `vx_ready_wait` after `vx_start`. The same
RTL passes in **simx, rtlsim, AND xrtsim with `DEBUG=3`/`DBG_TRACE_AFU` —
all three software simulators show the AFU FSM transitioning correctly
(`STATE_IDLE → STATE_INIT → STATE_RUN → STATE_DONE → STATE_IDLE`)**, yet
on real hardware execution never completes.

This appears to be the same class of issue as **#262** (U250 hang at
`wait_for_completion`), **#263** (the explicit observation that "the
applications within the tests directory are primarily designed for
simulation environments and require significant modifications to run
correctly on actual FPGA hardware"), and **#278** (DECERR-related hang
where some users report ray24777's `+0x4000000000` AXI offset workaround
fixes it but bighead-liat reports the hang persists after applying it).

I'm filing this as a separate issue because my hardware (VCK5000 ES1
Versal) is different from #262/#263/#278 (U250 UltraScale+), I have a
specific working `STARTUP_ADDR` patch for the single-bank case that I'd
like to upstream, and the depth of diagnostic data may help maintainers
narrow down the framework issue across all these reports.

## Setup

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Hardware | Xilinx VCK5000 ES1 (Versal `xilinx_vck5000-es1_gen3x16_2_202020_1`) |
| OS | Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS |
| XRT | 2.11.648 (Branch 2021.1) |
| Vivado / Vitis | 2020.2 |
| Vortex master HEAD | `31e4765` (Oct 2025 squash, contains 87e613d2 deadlock fix and fce24b95 done handshake fix) |
| Branch | `fix/vck5000-support` (master + minimal VCK5000 patches) |
| Configurations tested | XLEN=64, NUM_CORES={2,4}, NUM_WARPS={4,8}, L2 {on,off}, drain logic {add,revert} |

## Symptom

Identical hang behavior across **4 independent bitstreams** built at
different points in our iteration (`test1`, `test2`, `test4`, `test7`):

```
$ make -C tests/regression/basic run-xrt
open device connection
info: device name=xilinx_vck5000-es1_gen3x16_base_2, memory_capacity=0x100000000 bytes, memory_banks=1.
number of points: 1024
buffer size: 4096 bytes
allocate device memory
allocating bank0...
reusing bank0...
dev_src=0x10000
dev_dst=0x11000
run memcopy test
write source buffer to local memory
read destination buffer from local memory
verify result
upload time: 0 ms
download time: 0 ms
Total elapsed time: 0 ms                            ← memcopy passes (host↔BO)
run kernel test
Upload kernel binary
reusing bank0...
upload kernel argument
reusing bank0...
start execution                                     ← hangs here forever
```

`xbutil examine` reports the CU as `IDLE` with `Usage=0` indefinitely.

The hang occurs **regardless of**:
- Kernel ELF entry address (tested `0x80000000` and `0x00100000`, same hang)
- Whether drain logic is present (`test4` has it, `test7` doesn't, both hang)
- Cores/warps (2c/4w through 4c/8w with L2)
- Build vintage (4 different bitstream builds spanning weeks)

## What I verified (RTL stack is functionally correct)

Same kernel binary, same host binary, three simulator backends, all PASS:

| Backend | Result | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| **simx** | ✅ PASS | Functional C++ simulator |
| **rtlsim** | ✅ PASS | Verilator, simple wrapper |
| **xrtsim with `DEBUG=3 DBG_TRACE_AFU`** | ✅ **PASS** | Verilator with **full XRT AFU wrap** (`VX_afu_wrap.sv` + `VX_afu_ctrl.sv`) |

The xrtsim trace shows the AFU FSM transitioning correctly:

```
[VXDRV] DCR_WRITE: addr=0x1, value=0x80000000   ← STARTUP_ADDR0
[VXDRV] DCR_WRITE: addr=0x2, value=0x0          ← STARTUP_ADDR1
[VXDRV] DCR_WRITE: addr=0x3, value=0x0          ← STARTUP_ARG0
[VXDRV] DCR_WRITE: addr=0x4, value=0x0          ← STARTUP_ARG1
               28657: AFU: Begin initialization              ← STATE_IDLE → STATE_INIT
               28673: AFU: Initialization completed          ← vx_reset deasserted
               28683: AFU: Begin execution                   ← vx_busy → STATE_RUN
               31445: AFU: Execution completed               ← STATE_RUN → STATE_DONE
               36561: AFU: Processor idle                    ← STATE_DONE → STATE_IDLE (after ap_done_ack)
PERF: instrs=81, cycles=801, IPC=0.101124
Test PASSED
```

This implies the RTL source (including the squash-included `87e613d2`
"fixed XRT AFU deadlock on exit" and `fce24b95` "fixed XRT AFU done
handshake" fixes) is **functionally correct** for the XRT control plane.
The bug is in the synthesis-to-silicon layer.

## What I ruled out

| Hypothesis | Verdict | Evidence |
|------------|---------|----------|
| RTL source bug (logic error) | ❌ REJECTED | 3 simulators PASS the same RTL |
| Our `STARTUP_ADDR` patch wrong | ❌ REJECTED | Verified in 3 sims; ELF inspection confirms |
| Kernel ELF address out of bank | ❌ REJECTED | Tested 0x100000 (1 MB) and 0x80000000 (2 GB), both hang same way |
| Drain logic add/remove | ❌ REJECTED | Both `test4` (drain in) and `test7` (drain out) hang identically |
| Bitstream construction race | ❌ REJECTED | 4 independent builds, identical symptom |
| `PLATFORM_MEMORY_OFFSET` mismatch | ❌ REJECTED | `xclbinutil --info` confirms DDR4 base = `0xC000000000` matches `platforms.mk` |
| `m_axi_mem_0` connectivity | ❌ REJECTED | xclbin shows `m_axi_mem_0 → MC_NOC0 (MEM_DDR4)`, range `0xFFFFFFFF` |
| Host MMIO control plane broken | ❌ UNLIKELY | `dev_caps`, `isa_caps`, `mem_capacity` all return correct values; `CTL_AP_RESET` writes work (init succeeds) |
| Setup timing | ✅ MET | WNS=+0.204 ns (test4), +0.023 ns (test7), 0 failing endpoints |
| Hold timing | ✅ MET (thin) | WHS=+0.030 ns, 0 failing endpoints — but margin is 30 ps |

## What I tried to fix on our end

1. **`STARTUP_ADDR` for single-bank platforms** (1-line fix in
   `tests/regression/common.mk`):

   ```diff
   - STARTUP_ADDR ?= 0x180000000
   + STARTUP_ADDR ?= 0x80000000
   ```

   The default `0x180000000` (6 GiB) was tuned for multi-bank Alveo cards
   (U50/U280: 8 GiB virtual window from 32 banks; U250/U200: 64 GiB from
   4 banks of 16 GiB each), but VCK5000's single-bank `ADDR_WIDTH=32`
   topology gives a 4 GiB virtual window — `0x180000000` doesn't fit, so
   `get_bank_info()` returned `index=1` for `num_banks=1` and the
   c4bcdc5/`>=` validator rejected it.

   `0x80000000` (2 GiB) fits in every supported board's virtual window
   (VCK5000/zynquplus: 4 GiB; U50/U280: 8 GiB; U250/U200: 64 GiB), so
   this is a universally safe lowering. Linker scripts already accept
   `--defsym=STARTUP_ADDR=...` from the makefile via
   `kernel/scripts/link{32,64}.ld:12`.

   **This patch is correct** (verified in 3 sims) but **does not fix the
   FPGA hang**.

2. **`ap_reset` priority over `ap_start` in `VX_afu_ctrl.sv`** —
   prioritized ap_reset bit (4) over ap_start bit (0) on AP_CTRL writes
   to prevent a race when host writes both bits in one cycle. This patch
   is in our local `c4bcdc5` and is needed but doesn't fix the hang
   either.

3. **Drain logic in `VX_afu_wrap.sv`** — added a workaround that drives
   `m_axi_mem_*ready_a = 1` and masks `m_axi_mem_*valid_vx = 0` during
   `vx_reset` to consume stale NoC responses. We later reverted this
   because it didn't help — the hang occurs both with and without it.

4. **Lowering `STARTUP_ADDR` further** to `0x00100000` (1 MB) to test
   whether the kernel ELF address mattered. Same hang.

5. **`PLATFORM_MEMORY_ADDR_WIDTH=34`** to extend the virtual window. **Timing
   FAILED**: WNS = `-0.400 ns`, **815 failing endpoints**, dominant
   critical path is the L2 cache `g_tag_store[6]` BRAM read → tag
   compare → `g_data_store[6]` BRAM write enable. Don't recommend this
   path for single-cycle cache designs.

## Cross-references

- **#262** (yonghun, U250, Jul 2025): identical "hangs at
  `wait_for_completion`" symptom after working around bank 0 issue.
- **#263** (yonghun, follow-up): the key observation that "in contrast,
  running the same applications with `TARGET=sim` (using xrtsim or
  verilator) does not exhibit these memory or buffer-related errors." We
  see exactly this.
- **#278** (steve+ray24777+bighead-liat, U250): the workaround
  `+ 64'h4000000000` to AXI master address calculation in
  `VX_afu_wrap.sv:289-292` resolves DECERR for some users but
  bighead-liat reports the demo "still doesn't finish execution on
  hardware (it hangs waiting for the kernel to complete)" after applying
  it — same as us. Worth noting that `xclbinutil --info` on our VCK5000
  bitstream shows `Base Address: 0xc000000000` matching our
  `PLATFORM_MEMORY_OFFSET=40'hC000000000`, so we don't seem to need the
  same offset adjustment, but the post-fix hang is identical.

## Diagnostic data

### xclbin memory configuration (test4, all bitstreams identical)

```
Memory Configuration
   Type:         MEM_DDR4
   Base Address: 0xc000000000
   Address Size: 0x200000000        # 8 GiB physical DDR
   Bank Used:    Yes

Ports
   Port:          m_axi_mem_0
   Range (bytes): 0xFFFFFFFF        # 4 GiB AXI master window
   Port Type:     addressable

Argument: MEM_0
   Port:    m_axi_mem_0
   Memory:  MC_NOC0 (MEM_DDR4)
```

### Routed timing summary

```
test4 (XLEN=64, ADDR_WIDTH=32, no L2):
  WNS=+0.204 ns  TNS=0  WHS=+0.030 ns  THS=0  All constraints met.

test7 (XLEN=64, ADDR_WIDTH=32, L2 enabled):
  WNS=+0.023 ns  TNS=0  WHS=+0.030 ns  THS=0  All constraints met (very thin).

test5 (XLEN=64, ADDR_WIDTH=34, L2 enabled):  ← abandoned
  WNS=-0.400 ns  TNS=-174 ns  815 failing endpoints  DO NOT USE.
```

### dmesg around xclbin load (no errors)

```
xocl 0000:0a:00.1: icap_lock_bitstream: bitstream 7c720838-... locked, ref=1
xocl 0000:0a:00.1: kds_add_context: Client pid(...) add context CU(0xffffffff) shared(true)
xocl 0000:0a:00.1: kds_del_context: Client pid(...) del context CU(0xffffffff)
xocl 0000:0a:00.1: icap_unlock_bitstream: bitstream 7c720838-... unlocked, ref=0
```

No DMA errors, no AFU/PCIe errors during the hang.

### `strace -p <basic pid>` during hang

The host process is in a tight polling loop reading `MMIO_CTL_ADDR`
(presumably looking for `CTL_AP_DONE` bit) via `xrtKernelReadRegister`.
No errors, no progress.

## Working tree state

```
modified:   hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv      # drain logic reverted to upstream master state
modified:   hw/syn/xilinx/xrt/vitis.ini        # commented sp= lines added (no effect)
modified:   tests/regression/common.mk         # STARTUP_ADDR patch (proposed)
```

`hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv` is **identical to upstream master**
(`origin/master`'s `31e4765`). `hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_ctrl.sv` has only
the `ap_reset` priority fix on top of upstream. So we're effectively
testing the **latest upstream Vortex master** on VCK5000 ES1, with minimal
patches.

## What I'd like to know

1. **Has anyone successfully run a Vortex regression kernel end-to-end on
   VCK5000 (any variant) on actual hardware**, or is the platform mostly
   tested via xrtsim only?

2. **Has anyone successfully run a Vortex regression kernel end-to-end on
   any Alveo board with the current master?** The ratio of "works in
   sim" to "hangs on FPGA" reports in the issue tracker is concerning.

3. **Is there a known set of patches** (not yet upstreamed to master)
   that fixes the FPGA-side hang? I noticed the commit history was
   squashed in `31e4765` (Oct 2025); side branches like `develop`,
   `bug_fixes`, `volt`, etc. have additional commits but I couldn't
   identify which ones target this hang.

4. **Would `report_timing -hold -delay_type max` on the corner conditions
   reveal anything STA missed?** Our WHS is +0.030 ns which feels
   suspiciously thin, and `xrtsim` doesn't model timing.

5. **Does the AFU control plane (`s_axi_ctrl`) need any specific
   `axi_clock_converter` configuration on Versal NoC?** We rely on v++
   to insert it automatically; maybe ES1 needs something explicit.

6. **The `STARTUP_ADDR` lowering patch above** — is there any reason
   *not* to lower it to `0x80000000` for all XLEN=64 builds? It works on
   every supported board's virtual window and removes the silent
   single-bank failure mode. Happy to submit a PR if welcome.

I'm willing to share the full xrtsim trace, all four bitstreams' timing
and utilization reports, and run any additional debug builds if it would
help maintainers narrow down the issue. Thanks for reading.

---

## Files I can attach if helpful

- Full xrtsim DEBUG=3 trace (~50 KB)
- All 4 bitstreams' `impl_1_hw_bb_locked_timing_summary_routed.rpt`
- All 4 bitstreams' `impl_1_hw_bb_locked_utilization_placed.rpt`
- xclbin info dumps (`xclbinutil --info`)
- Working tree diff vs `origin/master`
- Host strace during the hang

comments.body:
## Update: XLEN=32 also hangs — framework bug independent of data-path width

Additional bitstream tested today: `test_32` — same 4-core / 8-warp / L2
configuration as `test7` but built with **XLEN=32** instead of 64.

### Build

```
XLEN=32, NUM_CORES=4, NUM_WARPS=8, L2_ENABLE=1,
PLATFORM_MEMORY_ADDR_WIDTH=32, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NUM_BANKS=1
```

Synthesis completed cleanly — timing met but margins are razor-thin:

```
WNS(ns)   TNS(ns)   TNS Failing   WHS(ns)   THS(ns)   THS Failing
+0.000    0.000     0             +0.030    0.000     0
```

`+0.000 ns` WNS is concerning but all constraints are technically met.

### Runtime behavior — identical hang

```
open device connection
info: device name=xilinx_vck5000-es1_gen3x16_base_2, memory_capacity=0x100000000 bytes, memory_banks=1.
...
run memcopy test
write source buffer to local memory
read destination buffer from local memory
verify result
upload time: 0 ms
download time: 0 ms
Total elapsed time: 0 ms                    ← memcopy OK
run kernel test
Upload kernel binary
reusing bank0...
upload kernel argument
reusing bank0...
start execution                             ← hangs here
```

`xbutil` reports the CU as `IDLE` with `Usage=0`, same as the other
bitstreams. `kernel.elf` linked at `Entry=0x80000000` (XLEN=32 default,
no STARTUP_ADDR patch required for this build).

### Updated diagnostic matrix

| Bitstream | XLEN | Cores/Warps | L2 | ADDR_WIDTH | Drain logic | WNS | FPGA result |
|-----------|------|-------------|----|-----------:|:-----------:|-----|-------------|
| test1 (old) | 64 | 2/4 | No | 32 | N/A | — | ❌ HANG |
| test2 | 64 | 2/4 | No | 32 | N/A | — | ❌ HANG |
| test4 | 64 | 4/8 | No (env var bug) | 32 | in | +0.204 | ❌ HANG |
| test5 | 64 | 4/8 | Yes | **34** | in | **-0.400** | N/A (815 failing endpoints) |
| test7 | 64 | 4/8 | Yes | 32 | reverted | +0.023 | ❌ HANG |
| **test_32** | **32** | 4/8 | Yes | 32 | reverted | **+0.000** | ❌ **HANG** |

**5 independent bitstreams, 6 different configurations, 100% identical
hang at `vx_ready_wait` on the same FPGA host.** All of:

- XLEN (32 vs 64)
- L2 cache enabled vs disabled
- Core/warp count (2c/4w vs 4c/8w)
- Drain logic in `VX_afu_wrap.sv` (present in test4, absent in test7/test_32)
- Kernel ELF entry address (`0x80000000` vs `0x180000000` vs `0x100000`)
- Bitstream build vintage (spanning weeks of iteration)

...are ruled out as root cause.

### Next experiment in progress

Currently synthesizing a variant with `-DRESET_DELAY=256` (default is 8
cycles in `hw/rtl/VX_config.vh:243`) to test whether the inner Vortex
reset network needs more than 8 cycles to settle on real Versal silicon.
Our hypothesis: simulators model reset as zero-delay, so an 8-cycle hold
is sufficient, but the synthesized reset tree on the actual FPGA may
have buffer / fanout delays that leave state machines deep in the cache
controllers in invalid states when `vx_reset` deasserts, causing
`vx_busy` to never assert and the AFU FSM to stay wedged in `STATE_INIT`.

Will report back when the `test_RST256` bitstream finishes
(~22:30 KST, ~2.5h from now).

### Note on `fce24b95` / `87e613d2` — already included

I verified that the upstream master squash commit `31e4765` includes
both:

- `87e613d2` "fixed XRT AFU deadlock on exit" (`VX_axi_write_ack.sv` +
  `vx_pending_writes` rework)
- `fce24b95` "fixed XRT AFU done handshake" (4-state FSM, `ap_ctrl_read`,
  `ap_done_ack` gating)

by direct file inspection (`git show origin/master:hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv`).
So these fixes are already in effect in all the bitstreams tested above
— they are *not* the missing piece.

Closing as superseded.

This report targets the pre-rewrite AFU control FSM (`STATE_IDLE → INIT → RUN → DONE`), which no longer exists — the AFU launch/completion path was rewritten to the Command-Processor model on current master.

The underlying real-hardware hang is a **timing-closure** issue, not a framework bug. As your own report noted (razor-thin `WNS +0.000 ns`), the bitstream barely met / did not meet timing at 300 MHz. A design that misses setup timing latches bad data and can wedge on real silicon while passing in simx / rtlsim / hw_emu (which don't model timing) — we've since reproduced exactly this and traced it to negative WNS on the kernel clock.

Action: rebuild on the current CP-based AFU with timing met (WNS ≥ 0). Please reopen with a fresh trace if a timing-clean build still hangs. Closing.

title: Problem with package pkg_scala2hdl when simulating created processor in VHDL
body:
Hi,

from the vexrisc description `VexRiscvWB_small` shown below (small cpu, wishbone bus, external interrupts) a vhdl-model can be generated without errors. But when simulation the model in Modelsim I got the following error message: 
```
#** Fatal: (vsim-3734) Index value 0 is out of range 1 to 2.
#    Time: 0 ps  Iteration: 0  Process: /vexriscvwb_top_tb/DUT/MCU/CPU/line__2183 File: VexRiscv.vhd
# Fatal error in Subprogram pkg_extract at VexRiscv.vhd line 193
```

The error message is due to the fist function `pkg_extract` in package `body pkg_scala2hdl`, which is part of the generated vhdl file:
```
  function pkg_extract (that : std_logic_vector; bitId : integer) return std_logic is
  begin
    return that(bitId);
  end pkg_extract;
```
This function does not renumber the elements of the parameter vector `that`.
Thus I changed the function to the following code which eliminates the error:
```
  function pkg_extract (that : std_logic_vector; bitId : integer) return std_logic is
    variable ret : std_logic_vector(that'length-1 downto 0);
  begin
    ret := that;
    return ret(bitId);
  end pkg_extract;
```
As far as I see now my system works correctly. 
Is this the correct way to fix the error? If yes, maybe the package `pkg_scala2hdl` should be changed.

title: When FS is 0 and a fld/fsd specific instruction causes an exception, there is a problem with the value of the mtval register
body:
**Describe the bug**

When the FS field in the mstatus register is 0, executing the `fld fa0, 288 (sp)` instruction causes an illegal instruction exception, and the values ​​of the xiangshan and nemu `mtval` registers are inconsistent.

Specifically, the value of the `xiangshan` mtval register is the machine code of the fld fa0, 288 (sp) instruction. 
The value of the mtval register in nemu is `0x00003512`

**To Reproduce**

```
.section .text
.globl _start
_start:
    li     t0, 0x8000000a00100a00     #FS: 00
    csrw    mstatus, t0 
    fld     fa0, 288(sp)
```


**Error log or Screenshots**

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef530af8-8bf7-4945-a792-7fe940b3a1bf)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41eb772e-9dd9-476c-b786-7849024df991)

When I use spike for debugging, the instruction corresponding to `0x00003512` is `c.fldsp fa0, 288 (sp)`. After testing, the `fsd `command also has this situation

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87563ceb-6e3b-429d-ae39-51ba54636cd1)


**Necessary information on versions**
- NEMU version: 34ba2259558ed89f5a042179ef0a9131e53ce037 (HEAD, origin/master, origin/HEAD)

fix_commits.messageHeadline: fix(CSR,RVC): c.fp instrs should be illegal when fs is off (#3859)

comments.body:
Thank you for your issue.
This is actually a bug in XiangShan.
The instruction `fld fa0, 288(sp)` was compiled into a compressed instruction `0x3512` under the C extension.
In XiangShan, the frontend decoding process expands the 16-bit C extension compressed instruction into a 32-bit instruction.
After that, it detects that FS is set to 0, so it stores the expanded instruction in mtval, rather than the original instruction itself.
This issue is currently being fixed by @sinceforYy

title: [BUG] CV-X-IF result transaction is ignored for offloaded instruction not writing back to the RF
body:
### Bug Description

While testing CV32E20 with a coprocessor supporting multiple in-flight instructions, I noticed that the CV-X-IF Result transaction is ignored in those cases where the offloaded instruction does not write back a value to the core's register file (i.e., `x_issue_resp_i.writeback` not asserted). For such instructions, the `x_issue_resp_i.writeback` signal is used to allow the processor to proceed to the next instruction at issue time ([cve2_id_stage.sv#L292](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cve2/blob/98b0a20f647d6d63e599d3c65ecd1cdede5ec02d/rtl/cve2_id_stage.sv#L292)).

While this allows the core to execute new instructions in parallel to the offloaded one(s), it has some undesired side effects, detailed in the following sections.

### 1. Multiple offloaded in-flight instructions with the same ID
The mechanism described above allows two coprocessor instructions to be in-flight inside the coprocessor at the same time, provided that:
- The first instruction does not write back to the register file (`x_issue_resp_i.writeback == 1'b0`).
- The second instruction is successfully offloaded (`x_issue_ready_i && x_issue_resp_i.accept`) before the first one has completed execution (`x_result_valid_i`).

However, the two in-flight instructions are tagged with the same ID (0), since the `x_issue_req_o.id` is hardwired to `'0` in [cve2_id_stage.sv#L297](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cve2/blob/98b0a20f647d6d63e599d3c65ecd1cdede5ec02d/rtl/cve2_id_stage.sv#L297). This violates the CV-X-IF "Identification" [specs](https://docs.openhwgroup.org/projects/openhw-group-core-v-xif/en/latest/x_ext.html#identification):
> The id values for in-flight offloaded instructions are required to be unique.

and:
> An id ends being in-flight when one of the following scenarios apply:
>
> - the corresponding issue request transaction is retracted.
>
> - the corresponding issue request transaction is not accepted and the corresponding commit handshake has been performed.
>
> the corresponding result transaction has been performed.

Because the second instruction is offloaded before the Result transaction from the first instruction is received, it should be tagged with a different, unique ID (e.g., 1). This is usually easy to workaround in coprocessors since CVE2 always sends the commit transaction for the instruction being offloaded together with the issue transaction. However, this is suboptimal in those cases where the coprocessor keeps track of in-flight instructions with a scoreboard directly indexed by the instruction ID from the issue and commit interfaces.

### 2. The core does not always wait for coprocessor instructions completion
Not stalling the core when offloading instructions with no writeback events causes the result transaction from such instructions to be ignored, allowing the core to proceed indefinitely. This might lead to unwanted behaviour. An example is that a `wfi` instruction issued after a coprocessor instruction with no writeback value might cause the core to enter sleep before the coprocessor completes the execution of all the offloaded instructions. Another side consequence is that exceptions or interrupts may be processed before before the coprocessor (and potentially connected modules) is in a clean state.

## Proposed Solution
A possible lightweight solution was drafted with the help of @davideschiavone, and consists in the following additions to the core:
- An `[X_ID_WIDTH-1:0]` counter to increment the ID every time an instruction is offloaded. The ID is propagated in the `x_issue_req_o` and `x_commit_o` interfaces at issue time.
- An ID-indexed single-bit scoreboard to track in-flight offloaded instructions. The ID-th scoreboard entry is set upon successful instruction offloading (issue interface) and reset when the corresponding result transaction is used. Exceptions, interrupts, `wfi` instructions and similar events are allowed to proceed only once the scoreboard is empty.

Working on this solution is currently a low-priority for us, but we plan to open a PR to solve the issue as soon as we have the time.

comments.body: Hi @StMiky, thanks for the Issue.  Is this related to #300?

Hello @MikeOpenHWGroup! It's not directly related. This issue concerns instructions that do not write back their result to the core's RF (i.e., `x_issue_resp_i.writeback == 1'b0`). On the other hand #300, as far I understood, is about assuming that coprocessors keep their `x_issue_resp_i.writeback` stable until the result transaction takes place.

Still, they both require changes in how the core handles the result transaction request coming from the coprocessor (`x_result_valid_i` and `x_result_req_i`), so solving them together might be beneficial.

pin_bit_information is defined as

The pbi_t unconstrained array I think is the issue.

title: [BUG] : Decoder Bitmanip instructions
body:
### Is there an existing CVA6 bug for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing bug issues

### Bug Description

Hello, 
this is a RTL bug in the cva6 [Decoder](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/decoder.sv), the problem appears in this code 
![image](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/assets/110232072/225efdd5-2fa1-48e2-9665-f728ed32c501)

there's 2 problems here : 

1. there's no condition for [24:23] bits, according to the spec these should be always 0.
2. there's no else for illegal instruction if we didn't enter any if.

so if we try using a directed test to execute an ctz instruction with [24-23] != 0 , the RTL will execute it, that's the wrong behavior !!

So the default `demo.bin` build should no longer hit this Rocket issue. I think this can be closed. If a Rocket demo failure still reproduces on current LiteX, please reopen/provide a fresh reproducer, especially noting whether LTO was explicitly enabled.

title: Misaligned accesses to non-idempotent regions raise AddrMisaligned instead of AccessFault
body: ### Before start - [x] I have read the [RISC-V ISA Manual](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-isa-manual) and this is not a RISC-V ISA question. 我已经阅读过 RISC-V 指令集手册，这不是一个指令集本身的问题。 - [x] I have read the [XiangShan Documents](https://xiangshan-doc.readthedocs.io/zh_CN/latest). 我已经阅读过香山文档。 - [x] I have searched the previous issues and did not find anything relevant. 我已经搜索过之前的 issue，并没有找到相关的。 - [x] I have reviewed the commit messages from the relevant commit history. 我已经浏览过相关的提交历史和提交信息。 - [] I have reproduced the incorrect behaviors using the latest commit on the master branch. 我已经使用 master 分支最新的 commit 复现了不正确的行为。 ### Branch master (kunminghu-v2) ### Describe the bug When a misaligned load or store targets a non-idempotent memory region (MMIO / uncacheable I/O), XiangShan raises `loadAddrMisaligned` / `storeAddrMisaligned` exceptions. The RISC-V Privileged Specification (§3.6.1 "Idempotency PMAs") recommends that such accesses should raise `*AccessFault` exceptions. ### Spec Reference From the RISC-V Privileged Specification, §3.6.1 *Idempotency PMAs* (NOTE block): > Non-idempotent regions might not support misaligned accesses. Misaligned accesses to such regions **should** raise access-fault exceptions rather than address-misaligned exceptions, indicating that software should not emulate the misaligned access using multiple smaller accesses, which could cause unexpected side effects. ### Code Evidence **1. Load pipeline** (`src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/LoadUnit.scala`): ```scala // Line 1312-1314 // We will generate misaligned exceptions at mmio. val s2_real_exceptionVec = WireInit(s2_exception_vec) s2_real_exceptionVec(loadAddrMisaligned) := (s2_out.isMisalign || s2_out.isFrmMisAlignBuf) && s2_uncache ``` **2. Store pipeline** (`src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/StoreUnit.scala`): ```scala // Line 388 s1_out.uop.exceptionVec(storeAddrMisaligned) := s1_out.mmio && s1_in.isMisalign ``` And in S2: ```scala s2_out.uop.exceptionVec(storeAddrMisaligned) := s2_actually_uncache && (s2_in.isMisalign || s2_in.isFrmMisAlignBuf) && !s2_un_misalign_exception ``` **3. LoadMisalignBuffer** (`src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/lsqueue/LoadMisalignBuffer.scala`): ```scala exceptionVec(loadAddrMisaligned) := true.B ``` ### Expected behavior Per the spec recommendation, when a misaligned load or store targets a non-idempotent (MMIO / uncacheable I/O) region: - A misaligned **load** should raise `loadAccessFault` (exception code 5) instead of `loadAddrMisaligned` (exception code 4). - A misaligned **store** should raise `storeAccessFault` (exception code 7) instead of `storeAddrMisaligned` (exception code 6). ### Environment XiangShan branch:master XiangShan config:DefaultConfig ### To Reproduce N/A —sorry for no minimal reproducer yet. The issue was found via code inspection. ### Additional context _No response_

fix_commits.messageHeadline: fix(LoadUnit): raise af for unalign access on MMIO region (#5700)

title: Unable to synthesize the design in Vivado 2021.2
body:
Hi, I'm compling the design into Verilog with command `make PRJ=myproject BOARD=pynq STANDALONE=true` and with default settings. However, the compiled code contains some depth-1 array in the `EmbeddedTLBMD` module, and when I synthesize the code with Vivado 2021.2, it says `[Synth 8-2913] Unsupported Dual Port Block-RAM template for tlbmd_3_reg` and reasons to cause this error contains `Write port has constant address.` and `Only 1 word in RAM `. These are both true. Array `tlbmd_0` to `tlbmd_3` does have only one element and address input is constant (beacuse the entry count of the ITLB declared in [NutCore.scala](https://github.com/OSCPU/NutShell/blob/cf7963435b824106690152507bb9312c159b8d5e/src/main/scala/nutcore/NutCore.scala#L116) is only 4, so `depth of the array` = [TotalEntry / Ways](https://github.com/OSCPU/NutShell/blob/cf7963435b824106690152507bb9312c159b8d5e/src/main/scala/nutcore/mem/TLB.scala#L161) = 1).

A simple way to fix this problem is by manually adding a platform-specific attribute `ram_style` to these signals repectively, and set the values to `registers`, as follows, so the arrays can be implemented with registers. (I don't know if the line contains the attribute can be added without users' intervention (by Chisel comilers))
``` Verilog
  (* ram_style = "registers" *) 
  reg [120:0] tlbmd_0 [0:0];
```
The `ram_style` attribute is also abled to be set using elaberation-time constrains, however an additional XDC file is required in this situation. I'm not sure which is the most appropiate approach to solve the problem.


The following is `EmbeddedTLBMD` module in the generated code, and only the array `tlbmd_0` to `tlbmd_3` are related to the issue.
``` Verilog
module EmbeddedTLBMD(

comments.body:
Hello @Bill94l, thank you for reporting the issue.

I will take a look on it, and let you know.

As you can see, the write-back mode of the HPDcache is not yet officially supported on the CVA6 as there is no a corresponding configuration, so you may have some issues. But anyway, It should in principle work.

Ok, I diagnosed the issue but I did not yet fixed it. It is not a very simple one. It is an integration bug: hpdcache in WB mode within the CVA6.

It is a cache coherency issue between the Icache and the Dcache (HPDcache). The runtime in the v-tests (tests with virtual memory), modifies instruction segments. These modifications are done locally in the HPDcache (because of the write-back mode), and are not visible by the instruction cache unless the HPDcache is flushed (this is not required when in write-through mode because the memory is always updated on writes). The runtime explicitly does this using a fence.i instruction, but currently this instruction only requests an invalidation of the Icache with no flush of the Dcache.

I need to modify the CVA6 controller to issue a CMO flush operation to the HPDCache in case of a fence.i instruction, or find another clever way to keep both caches coherent... I have some ideas but I will think it over a little more.

You will need to be a little patient for this one.

Hi @Bill94l,

The fix is on its way. I have an opened Pull Request #2691 that fixes the coherency issue between the Icache and the Dcache when using the HPDcache in WB mode.

title: microwatt BIOS hangs in ISR
body:
With the current LiteX versions and the Microwatt CPU (`--cpu-type=microwatt --cpu-variant=standard+ghdl+irq`) the BIOS hangs in the ISR with what appears to be a wild jump to an invalid address outside of the memory space.  This in turn results in no console output and is repeatable in simulation.

I've attached a simulation trace database and the BIOS files generated from a Debian Bullseye ppc64le host system for analysis.  The last instructions executed appear to be as follows:

```
        /* Load IRQ handler address from SRAM */
        LOAD_IMM64(%r3, __isr_address)
    102c:       00 00 60 3c     lis     r3,0
    1030:       00 00 63 60     ori     r3,r3,0
    1034:       c6 07 63 78     rldicr  r3,r3,32,31
    1038:       00 00 63 64     oris    r3,r3,0
    103c:       00 00 63 60     ori     r3,r3,0
        ld      %r3,   0(%r3)
    1040:       00 00 63 e8     ld      r3,0(r3)

        mtctr   %r3,
    1044:       a6 03 69 7c     mtctr   r3
        mr      %r3, %r10
    1048:       78 53 43 7d     mr      r3,r10
        bctrl
    104c:       21 04 80 4e     bctrl

<jump to invalid address 0x4800002408000048>
```

comments.body: May be related to #1077
@shenki Any chance you might be able to take a look at this?

From what I can tell, objdump might be mistranslating `bctrl`, microwatt is processing that instruction as a `bcctr` (not sure which is correct right now, so I'm assuming microwatt is doing the right thing).

If true, the invalid jump is caused by `ld      r3,0(r3)` loading the data at 0x0 into r3, which is obviously incorrect.  Starting to suspect `__isr_address` might be wrong at this point.

Confirmed, `LOAD_IMM64(%r3, __isr_address)` is loading 0x0 (ROM base) instead of the correct location 0x100000 (SRAM base).

When run without IRQ support the console does come up, but there are residual issues that may be caused by related linking errors.  Will continue to debug here.

OK, it appears this has been an issue for quite a while and no one was testing, including on our side, as we were using a different boot firmware that takes advantage of the `SPR_KAISB` feature.

I'll be spending some time to apply https://gitlab.raptorengineering.com/kestrel-collaboration/kestrel-firmware/bootrom/-/merge_requests/10 to the LiteX tree and creating a new pull request once I know it's working...

Thanks @madscientist159, it's planned to add Microwatt testing to the CI (at it is currently done for most supported RISC-V CPUs), but this hasn't been done yet but we could put more efforts into this.

This should now be covered by current LiteX.

I also tested the Microwatt IRQ boot path locally with both:

  - `--cpu-variant=standard+irq`
  - `--cpu-variant=standard+ghdl+irq`

Both reached the LiteX BIOS prompt, so I can no longer reproduce the original ISR hang.

CI has also been updated with enjoy-digital/litex@de10ffc154a66c1798943f3070101d2825611061 so `test_cpu[microwatt]` now exercises the `standard+irq` variant directly.

I think this can now be closed. If an IRQ-specific Microwatt boot issue still reproduces on current LiteX, please open a fresh issue with the updated reproducer.

Hi ^^

Sorry for the delay i was AFK holiday XD

So, i pushed a fix for the GenCustomInterrupt demo via https://github.com/SpinalHDL/VexRiscv/commit/1746af1cfe11d0f75b6d3b4460c7d4a0ff8cf98f

(just have to have the CsrPlugin first in the list, that's not great, i would say even a bit flawed, but hooo well XD)

> I have second question. How can you choose to enable or not the 'A' instructions set ?

If you don't have memory coherency, you just need to turn on in the DataCacheConfig the following parameters : 
                           withLrSc = true
                           withAmo = true

Note that the atomic stay in the CPU, if you have another memory master it wont be atomic with that other memory master

**What is the expected behavior?**

Compilation successfully finishes and produces a system with a 256-bit external interface.  Tests can successfully run on the system.

**Please tell us about your environment:**
<!--    (examples)
    - version: `git commit hash`

**What is the use case for changing the behavior?**

Would like to increase the external memory interface bit width to provide more memory bandwidth to the system.  Setting the external memory interface bit width with `WithEdgeDataBits` to anything above 128-bits fails due to an issue in AXI4Fragmenter where an index into an address exceeds the overall bit width of the address.  The address index is dependent on beatBytes.  Printing out the slave.maxAddress in the AXI4Fragmenter seems to print addresses corresponding to devices that should not see this change in bit width (debug-controller and interrupt-controller devices).  However, printing out lgBytes shows that they are seeing this bit width change. These devices sit on buses internal to the system where the bit width is unchanged.  The debug-controller specifically is the device that causes the exception since its maxAddress can be represented with only 12-bits.  The shifting of this address by lgBytes produces a resulting bit vector that is too small to be indexed by the AXI len parameter (set to 8).

comments.body:
The problem is not what you explain above.

The problem is that the AXIMMIO simulation memory is only 4kB which is not larger than a full-sized AXI burst with a 256-bit bus.

In src/main/scala/subsystem/Ports.scala, change:
```
-      val mmio_mem = LazyModule(new SimAXIMem(edge, size = 4096))
+      val mmio_mem = LazyModule(new SimAXIMem(edge, size = 4096*2))
```

However, we probably want the AXI4Fragmenter to work also in this case, so I'll fix it instead.

comments.body:
There are two issues here.

First, you **must** use the riscv-tests that is found in `rocket-chip/riscv-tools/riscv-tests`. You can **not** use the master branch of riscv-tests. As one example, there was a privileged spec update from v2.0.1 to boom-devel so you must rebuild all of your riscv-tools on a BOOM update.

Second, on `devel` going forward, you **must** build a new compiler and specifically disable the Compressed Extension, since rv64imafdc is now the default compiler option. The `devel` readme describes how (https://github.com/ucb-bar/riscv-boom/blob/devel/README.md) under the "Installing the RISC-V Toolchain".
Thanks for fast reply. I'll try it this evening.

Latest developement commit : 3eb9560e93b6491cac9e4b1fc7fba499c02ba340
Boom branch : devel
Rocket branch : boom-devel.
Riscv-tools : commit from boom-devel branch of rocket without any checkouts,
compiled with --with-arch=rv64imafd.
Riscv-tests compile with recompiled riscv-tools.

Commands:
make run-bmark-tests CONFIG=MediumBoomConfig
make run-asm-tests CONFIG=MediumBoomConfig

Result: endless execution on tests
  benchmarks/mm.riscv
  rv64um-v-mul

I'll try v2.0.1 tag tomorrow (and may be v2.0 and v1.0, if it doesn't work).

I have reproduced the error on my end.

**Working Config:**
SmallBoomConfig

**BrokenConfigs:**
BOOMConfig
MediumBoomConfig
SmallBoomConfig with fWidth=2

Looks like I dropped the ball on testing superscalar fetch somehow.

Issue found. The method for detecting illegal instructions has changed -- decode bits are sent to the CSRFile and the CSRFile provides a Bundle of illegal signals (i.e., fp_illegal, system_illegal, etc.). 

However only one decode port is provided into the CSRFile. This breaks superscalar decode.
Fixed. Requires pull of boom `devel` branch and rocket-chip `boom-devel` branch.

title: cannot write with X-HEEP on FLASH into the data_flash_only section
body:
When mapping data to the X-HEEP data_flash_only section as in [this example](https://github.com/esl-epfl/x-heep/blob/main/sw/applications/example_spi_write/main.c#L236), the test fails as the values read back are all 0s.

By adding printf here and there in `iceprog`, I could see data being written correctly from the compiled `.hex` file.
Even when such `.hex` file gets modified by hand.

I noticed that the data written are above the file_size, as this does not take into account gaps into the address space.
by adding a "+1" [here](https://github.com/esl-epfl/x-heep/blob/main/sw/vendor/yosyshq_icestorm/iceprog/iceprog.c#L1014) 

```
for (int addr = begin_addr; addr < end_addr+1; addr += block_size) {
```

I erased one extra 64KB block to be sure to erase also data above the address that I wanted to write.

The values are mapped at address 0x10000, and `printf` into the `flash_prog` functions show that data are written as expected, and `printf` in the `flash_read` functions confirm that the data read are correct.

When running on X-HEEP instead, `prinft` into the `bsp` functions show that the address and data written are correct, but when reading, only values equal to `0` are read, failing the test.

Possible bugs are in `SW`, but I could not identify where (yet).

title: Murax debug on FPGA
body:
I had some success using Debug with verilator, now I switched to FPGA (iCE40-HX8K) and a  JLink JTAG probe. I am using the project [iCE40-hx8k_breakout_board](https://github.com/SpinalHDL/VexRiscv/tree/master/scripts/Murax/iCE40-hx8k_breakout_board).
**What works:**
- The code execution in general, without connection to debug I mean.
- The JTAG connection seems fine, the target is found everytime, I can read/write registers and run from the first instruction to the first breakpoint (which I can place anywhere in the code).

**What does not work:**
- I cannot step (just trying intruction level for now). when I try to instruction step from the first instruction, instead of jumping to 0x800000b0 I land at 0xb0. If I set a break point at 0x800000b0 and just run then I stop there. Then if I instruction step I land at 0xb4 instead of 0x800000b4... It seems the instruction step is discarding some most significant bits. 
- I cannot run to a second breakpoint

**What I tried:** 
- removing all break points -> the first instruction step still lands at 0xb0
- reduce JTAG frequency to 400kHz -> same behavior
- openocd debug message does not contain obvious error message

openocd_riscv is up-to-date, Murax is from yesterday, I just changed the RAM size to 8k (it is 4k in the object "MuraxWithRamInit").

One detail about the wiring: I connected only TMS,TDI,TDO,TCK,GND and VREF. I did not connect TRST to anything, should it be ?

title: [BUG] Combinational loop in hypervisor extension
body:
### Is there an existing CVA6 bug for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing bug issues

### Bug Description

The decoder (core/decoder.sv) does not assign a default value to signal 'tinst', when the hypervisor extension is enabled (CVA6Cfg.RVH). This leads to a combinational loop in some tool flows.
Assigning a default value at the beginning of: `always_comb begin : decoder` solves the problem.

title: [TTI] Spurious TX_DESC_STAT interrupt caused by virtual_device_sel_i gap on bus START
body: Hi i3c-core team, We're using [i3c-v1.5.0](https://github.com/chipsalliance/i3c-core/releases/tag/i3c-v1.5.0) and found spurious TX_DESC_STAT interrupt caused by virtual_device_sel_i gap on bus START **New version** i3c-core/src/hci/tti.sv: [line 427](https://github.com/chipsalliance/i3c-core/blob/db4a6f341145e05a5b7002a21d1cd5cc31147f35/src/hci/tti.sv#L427) `.irq_i (~virtual_device_sel_i & tx_pr_start_i), // Per-transaction flag` **The Race Condition** virtual_device_sel_i is **cleared on every Start condition** (i3c_target_fsm.sv, [line 871](https://github.com/chipsalliance/i3c-core/blob/db4a6f341145e05a5b7002a21d1cd5cc31147f35/src/ctrl/i3c_target_fsm.sv#L871) ): ``` else if (bus_any_start_det || bus_stop_det_i) begin virtual_device_sel_o <= '0; // ← Clears on Start! ``` On every bus START condition, virtual_device_sel_o is forced to 0. It only reasserts after the FSM enters CheckFByte/CheckSByte and the address matches. During this multi-cycle gap, ~virtual_device_sel_i is 1, **which opens the interrupt gate and allows TX_DESC_STAT to fire spuriously if tx_pr_start_i is asserted**. **Waveform** Thanks, TJ

Hi @TJTseng 

What is the context of this use case in a system view? 

If it is in Caliptra's context, while streaming boot is ongoing, i3c interrupts are not enabled. The way streaming boot agent running on BMC would know to enumerate over mctp is after streaming boot is completed. It is after the streaming boot is done that the interrupts can be enabled as a part of indicating the completion of streaming boot. 

Since the MCTP that runs on one target is mutually exclusive with the recovery flow, as in streaming boot completes and then mctp starts, streaming boot transactions are not expected to come from the streaming boot agent (that runs on BMC or something equivalent of BMC) once Caliptra SS indicates the completion.

In summary, while this interrupt assertion is getting triggered, in the specific system flow where this is applied, there is no scenario that this becomes relevant. Having said that, it is an odd behavior that we will fix in future revision.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Hi @bharatpillilli ,
Thank you for the detailed explanation. Currently, we don't have this scenario in our system flow. We observed the odd behavior because we accidentally enabled TX_DESC_STAT_EN during recovery mode, so we reported this issue in case of any side effects. Our current approach is to disable TX_DESC_STAT_EN during recovery mode.

Let me summarize my understanding to make sure we're on the same page:
 Recovery / I3C streaming boot:
  - virtual_device_sel_i is active during this phase, and the transient deassertion on bus START creates the interrupt gating window
  - However, TX_DESC_STAT_EN should not be enabled during this phase, so the spurious interrupt does not fire

  MCTP (post-boot management communication):
  - Runs on the primary I3C target address, not the virtual target address
  - virtual_device_sel_i is not involved in MCTP transactions, so the gating issue does not apply

Are these correct?

Thanks,
TJ

@TJTseng 

Your assumptions are correct. 

We are marking this as a feature enhancement since interrupts are not supposed to be enabled during recovery flow. This enhancement will be in our next I3C release. Please make sure to follow these guidelines:

1. During recovery mode they shall be no private reads/writes to the main target
2. During recovery mode FW must disable interrupts (including TX_DESC_STAT)
3. When exiting recovery mode FW must clear TX_DESC_STAT interrupts.
     a. Once recovery mode has been exited the controller shall not issue any OCP recovery commands - there is not live status to read.

This enhancement has been integrated into the v1p6 branch https://github.com/chipsalliance/i3c-core/pull/217

I will close this issue in 1 week pending any additional questions.

title: dragonphy wants adk/multivt regardless of full_chip default view
body:
Our default for full_chip build is currently to use adk view `stdview`, as specified in `full_chip/construct.py`:
```
  adk_name = 'tsmc16'
  adk_view = 'stdview'
```
Unfortunately, this breaks the final LVS because our separately-built dragonphy uses LVT cells that do not exist in `stdview`
```
% calibre -lvs ...
Error: No matching ".SUBCKT" statement for "DEL100D1BWP16P90LVT" ...
Error: No matching ".SUBCKT" statement for "DEL200D1BWP16P90LVT" ...
Error: No matching ".SUBCKT" statement for "BUFFSKND1BWP16P90LVT" ...
...
```
Seems like there should be an easy/obvious solution to this problem, but I have not yet been able to discover it. Among the ideas I have come up with so far:

* change `full_chip/construct.py` to use `multivt` for everything, so the needed libraries will be available when/if needed
```
full_chip/construct.py:
  < adk_name = 'tsmc16'
  < adk_view = 'stdview'
  ----------------------
  < adk_name = 'tsmc16'
  > adk_view = 'multivt'
```
* use pre_extend_commands to change lvs `inputs/adk` link from `stdview` to `multivt`
```
full_chip/construct.py:
  lvs.pre_extend_commands( [
    'pushd inputs; unlink adk; ln -s ../../12-tsmc16/multivt adk; popd'
  ] )
```
* make a new `custom-lvs` node that links `multivt` instead of `stdview`

* parameterize adk for lvs node, e.g. similar to what was done with `lvs_hcells_file`, included below for comparison...
```
mflowgen/steps/mentor-calibre-lvs/lvs.runset.template:
    *lvsHCellsFile: ${lvs_hcells_file}
  - *cmnV2LVS_SPICEIncFiles: inputs/adk/*.cdl inputs/*.spi inputs/*.sp
  + *cmnV2LVS_SPICEIncFiles: ${adk}/*.cdl     inputs/*.spi inputs/*.sp

mflowgen/steps/mentor-calibre-lvs/configure.yml:
     lvs_hcells_file: ""
  +  lvs_adk            : "inputs/adk"

full_chip/construct.py:
    'lvs_hcells_file'   : 'inputs/adk/hcells.inc',
  + 'lvs_adk'           : 'inputs/adk/../multivt',
```

For now I'm using option 1, since it was the easiest to do initially. Looking at it now, I'm thinking the final option in the list (`lvs_adk` parameter) is probably the best, as it kind of goes along with existing flow -- `lvs.runset.template` is already fairly heavily parameterized.

Thoughts?

title: [BUG] DIV request lost following flush causing hang in simulation
body: ## Observed behavior The test executed is `fpu_op_group_test.svh` and `seed=1760627103` (`OP_GROUP=DIVSQRT`, `fmt inside {FP32, FP64, FP16}`) in [cvfpu-uvm](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu-uvm). During this test, random division and square-root requests are issued, with a flush-on-the-fly randomly asserted during execution. The following sequence is observed as shown in the waveform: 1. Request A is accepted by the DUT. 2. A flush is asserted on the next clock cycle while request A is still in-flight. 3. Request B is sent after the flush. 3. The testbench waits indefinitely for a response for request B and the simulation hangs. ## Root cause The affected unit is `fpnew_divsqrt_th_64_multi.sv`, the wrapper around the C910 T-Head div/sqrt unit. Specifically, the `func_sel` and `op_sel` registers, which are two pulses that trigger the launch of the div/sqrt execution, are not cleared on flush: https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/3eb6afeab2cb33f7d8689222955d0171aeb3a801/src/fpnew_divsqrt_th_64_multi.sv#L336-L342 Since these pulses are not cleared by flush, a flush occurring between request acceptance and the actual launch of execution leaves the unit in an inconsistent state, causing subsequent requests to hang.

title: Error while generating the frontend with setuptools >= 81.0.0
body:
While trying to generate the frontend of the iDMA for the MAGIA platform, I faced the following error:
```
from pkg_resources import resource_filename
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pkg_resources'
```

This error is related to `regtool`, specifically to the `gen_dv.py` script where there's the mentioned import. Checking online, `pkg_resources` became deprecated and was removed from `setuptools` in versions `>=81.0.0`.

I'm opening this issue just to document the problem, downgrading `setuptools` to version `80.0.0` solves it.

To reproduce the error (tested with Python 3.12):
```sh
git clone https://github.com/pulp-platform/iDMA.git
python3 -m venv idma-venv
source idma-venv/bin/activate
pip3 install -r requirements.txt
make idma_hw_all IDMA_ADD_IDS=rw_axi_rw_obi
```
